name: Computer Science, B.S.
affiliationText: At least C (not C–) in all completed CS courses and critical math courses. GPA ≥2.5 in CS/ENGRD 2110/2112 and CS 2800/2802. A required supplemental application must be submitted with the College of Engineering Major Affiliation application.

electiveGroups.name: Liberal Studies
electiveGroups.description: Courses from approved liberal arts and humanities distribution list.
electiveGroups.notes: Any approved liberal studies course outside engineering.

electiveGroups.name: Advisor-Approved Elective
electiveGroups.description: A course numbered 1100 or above that your faculty advisor approves.
electiveGroups.notes: Courses numbered 1100 and up count, except courses that come before where the engineering curriculum starts, such as MATH 1110, MATH 1900 and CS 1109. ROTC courses at the 3000 level or above may be accepted. Advisors usually approve extra liberal studies courses, extra ENGRI or ENGRD courses, communications courses and upper-level technical courses. Your faculty advisor approves each one, so check with them before registering.

electiveGroups.name: Engineering Distribution (second ENGRD)
electiveGroups.description: An Engineering Distribution course from a different category than CS 2110 (Scientific Computing).
electiveGroups.notes: The two ENGRD courses must come from two different categories. CS 2110 covers Scientific Computing, so this one comes from Materials, Mechanics, Probability and Statistics, Electrical Sciences, Thermodynamics, Earth and Life Sciences, or Biology and Chemistry.

electiveGroups.name: CS Elective (4000+)
electiveGroups.description: Two CS courses at the 4000 level or above. CS 3700 or CS 3780 counts if the other one fills the core.
electiveGroups.notes: Not CS 4090, 4997, 4998 or 4999. Must be at least 3 credits and taken for a letter grade.

electiveGroups.name: Practicum or Project Course
electiveGroups.description: One course from the CS department's practicum or project list.
electiveGroups.notes: 2 to 4 credits, letter grade. A practicum taken alongside its lecture (for example CS 4411 with CS 4410) counts here.

electiveGroups.name: Technical Elective
electiveGroups.description: A 3000+ course of at least 3 credits that has a qualifying prerequisite or corequisite. Every CS course of 3+ credits at 3000+ counts.
electiveGroups.notes: The list is built from the catalog's qualifying courses, prerequisite chains and the probability, statistics and biology text rules. At most two research courses (letter grade, 3+ credits) may count. Not CS 4090, 4997 or 4998.

electiveGroups.name: Technical Elective (2000-level allowed)
electiveGroups.description: The third technical elective, which may be a 2000-level course with a qualifying prerequisite or corequisite.
electiveGroups.notes: Same rules as the other technical electives, except one of the three may be numbered 2000 or above.

electiveGroups.name: External Specialization
electiveGroups.description: Three 3000+ courses of at least 3 credits in one topic area outside Computer Science.
electiveGroups.notes: The three must share a department prefix (e.g. MATH) or a topic a CS advisor approves; the app can't check that. At most one may be cross-listed with CS. No research, independent study, project team, PE or teaching credit.

electiveGroups.name: Major-Approved Elective
electiveGroups.description: Any course of at least 3 credits (or courses adding up to 3).
electiveGroups.notes: Letter grade or S/U. Not PE, ROTC below 3000, courses below 1100, or AP/IB credit.

electiveGroups.name: AI / Machine Learning Choice
electiveGroups.description: CS 3700 or CS 3780.

electiveGroups.name: Operating Systems Choice
electiveGroups.description: CS 4410 or CS 4414.

name: Electrical and Computer Engineering, B.S.
affiliationText: At least C+ in MATH 2930 or MATH 2940, PHYS 2213, and one of ECE/ENGRD 2100, ECE/ENGRD 2720, or ECE/ENGRD 2300. GPA ≥2.5 in listed core courses if completed.

electiveGroups.name: Liberal Studies
electiveGroups.description: Courses from approved liberal arts and humanities distribution list.
electiveGroups.notes: Any approved liberal studies course outside engineering.

electiveGroups.name: Advisor-Approved Elective
electiveGroups.description: A course numbered 1100 or above that your faculty advisor approves.
electiveGroups.notes: Courses numbered 1100 and up count, except courses that come before where the engineering curriculum starts, such as MATH 1110, MATH 1900 and CS 1109. ROTC courses at the 3000 level or above may be accepted. Advisors usually approve extra liberal studies courses, extra ENGRI or ENGRD courses, communications courses and upper-level technical courses. Your faculty advisor approves each one, so check with them before registering.

electiveGroups.name: Engineering Distribution (second ENGRD)
electiveGroups.description: An Engineering Distribution course from a different category than ENGRD/ECE 2300 (Electrical Sciences). ENGRD 2140 / ECE 2400 is recommended.
electiveGroups.notes: Advanced Programming: your ECE, ENGRD or advisor-approved courses must include ECE 2400/ENGRD 2140 (preferred) or CS/ENGRD 2110. The app doesn't check that yet.

electiveGroups.name: ECE Foundation: Fields or Microelectronics
electiveGroups.description: ECE 3030 or ECE 3150.
electiveGroups.notes: ECE foundation requirement (Cornell catalog 2026-27): at least 3 courses: one of 3030/3150, one of 3100/3250, and one more from the five.

electiveGroups.name: ECE Foundation: Probability or Signals
electiveGroups.description: ECE 3100 or ECE 3250.
electiveGroups.notes: ECE foundation requirement (Cornell catalog 2026-27): at least 3 courses: one of 3030/3150, one of 3100/3250, and one more from the five.

electiveGroups.name: Additional ECE Foundation Course
electiveGroups.notes: ECE foundation requirement (Cornell catalog 2026-27): at least 3 courses: one of 3030/3150, one of 3100/3250, and one more from the five.

electiveGroups.name: ECE Elective
electiveGroups.description: ECE courses at the 3000 level or above, including courses cross-listed with ECE and CS 4120, 4410, 6210, 4787, 4782 and 4789.
electiveGroups.notes: Not ECE 4999, 5830, 5870 or 5880. Foundation courses beyond the required three count here. The five ECE electives total at least 17 credits; the app doesn't check that total.

electiveGroups.name: ECE Elective (4000+)
electiveGroups.description: Two of the five ECE electives must be at the 4000 level or above.
electiveGroups.notes: Same rules as the other ECE electives, at 4000+. CS 4120, 4410 and their practica, CS 6210, 4787/5777, 4782/5782 and 4789/5789 count here.

electiveGroups.name: Culminating Design Experience
electiveGroups.notes: From ECE's requirements page (the catalog lists only five of these).

electiveGroups.name: Outside Technical Elective
electiveGroups.description: Non-ECE math, science or engineering courses at the 2000 level or above (1000-level only with a prerequisite). ECE 5830 counts.
electiveGroups.notes: 9 credits, at least 3 of them lecture at 3000+, letter grade. Not ENGRI, ENGRC or business courses, nor courses cross-listed with ECE. Up to 3 credits of project team or independent study. An engineering course must count as technical in its own major.

name: Mechanical Engineering, B.S.
affiliationText: At least C– in ENGRD 2020, ENGRD 2210 (if taken), and all completed required math, chemistry, physics, and CS courses. GPA ≥2.5 in MATH 2930, PHYS 2213, ENGRD 2020, and ENGRD 2210.

electiveGroups.name: Liberal Studies
electiveGroups.description: Courses from approved liberal arts and humanities distribution list.
electiveGroups.notes: Any approved liberal studies course outside engineering.

electiveGroups.name: Advisor-Approved Elective
electiveGroups.description: A course numbered 1100 or above that your faculty advisor approves.
electiveGroups.notes: Courses numbered 1100 and up count, except courses that come before where the engineering curriculum starts, such as MATH 1110, MATH 1900 and CS 1109. ROTC courses at the 3000 level or above may be accepted. Advisors usually approve extra liberal studies courses, extra ENGRI or ENGRD courses, communications courses and upper-level technical courses. Your faculty advisor approves each one, so check with them before registering.

electiveGroups.name: Technical Elective
electiveGroups.description: A technical course: engineering 2000+, MATH beyond 2940, PHYS beyond 2214, CHEM 2080 or beyond 2090, or biological sciences 2000+.
electiveGroups.notes: Not engineering economics, business, management, financial, teaching or organization courses (incl. MAE 4610, 4980); the app filters these by title, and your advisor has the final word. BIOG 1440/1445, BIOMG 1350, BIOEE 1610 and BIOSM 1610 count. ENGRG 3400 or research count at 3+ credits. No AP credit.

electiveGroups.name: Mathematics Elective
electiveGroups.description: One course from MAE's approved list: ENGRD 2700, CEE 3040, ENGRD/CEE 3200, ECE 3100, STSCI 2200, ECON 3110, ENGRD/ECE 2720 or CS 2800.
electiveGroups.notes: At least one elective must satisfy the probability and statistics requirement (every course here but ENGRD/CEE 3200 does); the app doesn't check that.

electiveGroups.name: Major Approved Elective
electiveGroups.description: Three courses from MAE's seven area lists (Aerospace, Biomechanics, Energy, Materials, Mechanical Systems and Design, Thermo-Fluids, Vehicle), at least 9 credits.
electiveGroups.notes: Not MAE 4610, 4900, 4980 or 4291. A 4xx1 senior-design version counts only if it isn't your senior design course. Major-program electives total 18+ credits, 9+ of them at 3000+; the app doesn't check those totals.

electiveGroups.name: Systems / Electronics Choice
electiveGroups.description: MAE 3780, ECE 2100, or PHYS 3360.

electiveGroups.name: Senior Design Elective
electiveGroups.description: MAE 4291 (3+ credits) or a 4-credit senior design elective.
electiveGroups.notes: Cornell catalog 2026-27. MAE 4441, 4641 and 4671 are also listed but not in the current catalog; add them when a roster-sync ingests them.

name: Operations Research and Engineering, B.S.
affiliationText: At least C in ENGRD 2700 and MATH 2940. GPA ≥2.2 in required math, science, engineering, and CS courses.

electiveGroups.name: Liberal Studies
electiveGroups.description: Courses from approved liberal arts and humanities distribution list.
electiveGroups.notes: Any approved liberal studies course outside engineering.

electiveGroups.name: Advisor-Approved Elective
electiveGroups.description: A course numbered 1100 or above that your faculty advisor approves.
electiveGroups.notes: Courses numbered 1100 and up count, except courses that come before where the engineering curriculum starts, such as MATH 1110, MATH 1900 and CS 1109. ROTC courses at the 3000 level or above may be accepted. Advisors usually approve extra liberal studies courses, extra ENGRI or ENGRD courses, communications courses and upper-level technical courses. Your faculty advisor approves each one, so check with them before registering.

electiveGroups.name: Math / Structures Choice
electiveGroups.description: MATH 2930, MATH 3040, or CS 2800.

electiveGroups.name: ORIE Elective
electiveGroups.description: ORIE courses at the 4000 level or higher (not a required major course, and not ORIE 4152, 5142, 5920, 5925 or 9000), plus ORIE 3320, 3741 and 3800.
electiveGroups.notes: At most 3 credits of ORIE 4990, and at most 3 credits between ORIE 4900, ORIE 4999 and CS 4999.

electiveGroups.name: Major Approved Elective (Category A)
electiveGroups.description: Category A (engineering, science and mathematics) courses on ORIE's approved list.
electiveGroups.notes: At least 6 of the 12 major-approved credits must be from Category A. At most 3 credits from ORIE 4900, 4990 and 4999 combined. Courses not on ORIE's list need a petition.

electiveGroups.name: Major Approved Elective (outside ORIE)
electiveGroups.description: Category A or B courses on ORIE's approved list, from outside ORIE.
electiveGroups.notes: At least 6 of the 12 major-approved credits must be from outside ORIE. Courses not on ORIE's list need a petition.
